## Goal
`SmtpImapMailer.scan_replies` (`engine/mail.py:375-384`) polls the mailbox until a link, an ID request or the deadline. If any single poll raises `MailError` (a dropped connection, a busy server) the exception leaves the loop at once, even with 9 minutes of the window left. The runner then treats the confirmation as not received. Keep polling inside the window: catch `MailError` from one poll, wait the normal interval, try again, and re-raise only if every poll in the window failed (the last error). A window of 0 seconds (`timeout_s=0`, as the runner uses, `engine/runner.py:729-732`) still makes exactly one attempt and behaves exactly as today.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. Fake `fetch_since`: fails, fails, then returns a message with a link: the scan returns that link (with a fake clock and `poll_interval_s` patched small).
2. All polls fail until the deadline: raises the last `MailError` (same message text as today).
3. `timeout_s=0`: exactly one call; a failure raises at once; success returns at once.
4. A `TlsPinError`-derived refusal (pin mismatch, `mail.py:367-368`) is NOT retried: it raises on the first poll (a wrong certificate must never be retried quietly).
5. Sleep time never exceeds the remaining window; no real sleeping in tests (monkeypatch `asyncio.sleep`).
6. `wait_for_confirmation` and the FakeMailer paths are unchanged; existing tests pass.
